title: Existence of invertible sheaves on a proper curve with prescribed vanishing of H^0 and H^1
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, on a proper curve over an algebraically closed field, an invertible sheaf L with one-dimensional H^0 and vanishing H^1, and an invertible sheaf N with vanishing H^0 and H^1. The proof of the first part is a descending induction on t = dim_k H^0(X, L): given a nonzero section s, it uses the nonempty open subset of nonsingular points to find a closed point x where s does not vanish, forms the ideal sheaf sequence 0 -> I tensor L -> L -> i_*i^*L -> 0, and analyses the resulting cohomology to reduce t by one (proof lines 10108-10149). H3: the reduction step through the point sequence and the control of the two cohomology groups is independent work, and the second part is obtained by twisting and using the first.
